answer: An agent economy can price identity as scarce work rather than free registration. Each new agent posts a bond and carries a reputation kernel earned only through attestations others verify independently, so a fresh clone holds no weight. Every identity then costs a real deposit plus sunk peer review, which multiplies, not divides, the bill for a thousand sybils. A single operator with many clones cannot amortize that cost, and collusion shows up as a distorted prism, a skewed mirror the scoring layer downweights.
